scope: local disposable-file and process fixtures for offline bundle inspection; no compiled validator execution
problem: The bundle inspection helper hashed the entire selected tool before checking its length and did not bind read-time file identity or executable permission.
change: Reuse the existing bounded regular-file executable fingerprint before invoking either selected bundle-inspection tool; failed reads return a path-free refusal.

verification.skipReason: Existing Linux-only process comm fixture; local development system is not Linux.

failedBeforeFix.scope: New assertions exercised before changing the inspection helper. Three reproduce unsafe admission/read ordering; one requires the new fingerprint error boundary.

observations: A file with executable permission removed refuses before invoking the process helper.
A wrong-length regular file refuses before either a buffered or descriptor open.
Replacing a selected file with a same-byte, same-mode file during hashing refuses before invocation.
An injected fingerprint I/O failure returns only REVIEWED_INSPECTION_TOOL_REQUIRED.
Existing real disposable-process checks still bound stdout/stderr, preserve path-free failure reporting and create no inspection log.

limitations: Checks use disposable fixture files and Python processes, not the compiled genesis auditor, keygen or validators.
The shared fingerprint implementation and runtime artifact pins are unchanged.
The binary directory still requires trusted operator control: later path-based execution is not atomically bound to the checked descriptor.
This changes only inspection-tool admission; it does not newly bound all bundle inputs or attest operator custody.
No new host admission, genesis compilation, bank replay, consensus or native transaction-history recovery is established.
